Explain the classification using feel and ribbon behaviour, and correct technique or moisture problems without copying an expected answer.

sourceBindings.text: Three safe, trainer-checked mineral soils representing contrasting sandy, clay-rich and loamy material; identity withheld until observation. No unverified potting-mix substitute.
Water spray bottle
Clean tray or flat work surface
Paper towels
Results sheet and pen
Ruler marked in centimetres
Task-appropriate gloves selected by the trainer
Each learner handles and records all three samples. Group roles do not replace individual performance.
Record length in cm at breakage and whether measured or estimated. No ball and no ribbon are valid recorded outcomes when technique and moisture have been checked.

sourceBindings.text: The conditioned sample holds a ball and makes a weak 1.8 cm ribbon. The wetter pinch feels very gritty.
The ball and ribbon outcomes rule out skipping directly to the no-ball branch.
The length enters the short-ribbon branch.
Very gritty feel leads to sandy loam, not simply loam because the ribbon is short.
Read the length branch and the feel branch together.

sourceBindings.text: The learner has checked for excessive dryness and wetness and used only material from the same sample. It still falls apart.
Record that it does not remain in a ball.
Do not add another soil, press indefinitely or invent a zero-length formed ribbon.
Follow the guide towards sand and retain the observations for the trainer.
A valid failed ball is evidence, not a failed learner.

sourceBindings.text: The sample forms a medium ribbon. Neither a gritty nor a very smooth sensation dominates the wetter-pinch check.
Record the measured 3.5 cm and the feel separately.
Follow the intermediate branch and then the neither-dominating branch.
The guide indicates clay loam; do not substitute the name loam from an inconsistent model table.
The observations take priority over a copied expected label.

sourceBindings.text: Trainer must verify safe mineral samples, protection and actual individual A/B/C handling. The linked crop item remains pending until S1-09; online answers and a group role do not pass it.
Prepare the workstation and keep A, B and C separately identified.
Observe A, take a palm-sized portion, remove debris and condition it gradually with water.
Try the ball; record valid non-formation after moisture checks rather than require every soil to hold a ball.
Use the correct ribbon method if a ball forms; otherwise record the valid branch and explain it.
Record A's observations before its classification and apply the complete length-plus-feel guide.
Clean between samples, then individually prepare and test B correctly.
Record and justify B's classification from its observations.
Clean between samples, then individually prepare and test C correctly.
Record and justify C's classification from its observations.
In the linked crop step, recommend and justify at least two candidates for each sample, including the practical card's minimum of one; keep this item pending until that evidence exists.
Clean hands, protection, materials and workstation and dispose of samples as instructed.

sourceBindings.text: Trainer must verify safe mineral samples, protection and actual individual A/B/C handling. The linked crop item remains pending until S1-09; online answers and a group role do not pass it.
Wear suitable task protection, including gloves, under the trainer's safe-sample procedure.
Take a representative small handful from the assigned sample and remove stones and debris.
Add water gradually and knead; check a ball or correctly record non-formation.
Form an even unsupported ribbon where the material allows it, or correctly explain the no-ribbon branch.
Record ribbon length and strength or absence, using the full guide rather than the simplified one-label rule.
Assess gritty versus smooth feel with the wet pinch.
State the field texture conclusion, evidence and any uncertainty.
Clean the workspace and dispose of material appropriately.
